On Jun 19, 2027, at 2:30 PM, Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> Team —
>
> Thanks Kris, forwarding Alex’s info below. Before I confirm the slots I want to sync quickly on scope/leveling so we evaluate consistently.

Quick notes from me (anchors + practical prompts):

Leveling guidance:
- Senior (IC4-ish): owns medium-to-large components, consistently delivers within a team, shows reliable tradeoff judgment, can lead a cross-team rollout but not set org-level strategy.
- Principal signals: defines end-to-end runtime architecture, owns cross-org infra tradeoffs, influences model- and infra-level kernel/compilation choices.

Debrief anchors (score 1–4 per area, where 3 is bar):
- System thinking & tradeoffs (design clarity, alternatives considered)
- Depth on performance levers (profiling, batching, KV cache, quantization effects)
- Ownership & execution (incidents handled, rollout evidence, mentoring)
- Code-level reasoning (debugging approach, testing/CI strategy)

Red flags (fail):
- Cannot reason about latency sources or propose measurable mitigations
- No evidence of rolling changes safely in prod (feature flags, canary metrics)
- Repeatedly conflates infra constraints with product requirements (no prioritization)

Practical prompts for interviews:
- System design: "Design a serving runtime to reduce tail latency by 20% for a 4B model under mixed RPS. What metrics and knobs do you expose?"
- Performance: "You see a 3x token-time regression in a quantized path — how do you triage?"
- Ownership: "Tell us about an incident you led; how did you identify root cause and what were the postmortem actions?"

Time budgets: 45–60 min per deep interview; please aim for 10–15 min of focused debrief notes immediately after. I’ll act as bar-raiser for final loop if we want a single bar-raise step.

— Markus
Markus Klein | Principal, Inference Runtime
